items.title: Section: The Third Yogic Process Opens

items.zh: 如是已說補特伽羅品類、建立及所緣等，乃至趣修有果、無果。如應安立，我今當說。總嗢柁南曰：往慶問、尋求、方安立：護養、出離、一境性、障淨、修作意。
items.en: Thus far has been explained the kinds of practitioners, their establishment, and their objects of meditation, up to the causes of setting out towards cultivation with or without fruit. How yogic practice should rightly be established, I shall now explain. The summary verse says: going, being welcomed, being questioned, and seeking — then the establishing, the safeguarding, the seclusion, the one-pointedness — the purification of obstructions, and the cultivation of mental engagement.

items.title: Travelling to the Teacher: Four Abiding Thoughts

items.zh: 若有自愛補特伽羅初修業者，始修業時，為隨證得自義利故，先應四處安住正念，然後往詣善達瑜伽或軌範師、或親教師、或餘尊重、似尊重所。云何四處？一、專求領悟，無難詰心處；二、深生恭敬，無憍慢心處；三、唯求勝善，非顯己能處；四、純為安立自他善根，非求利養恭敬名聞處。
items.en: If there is a self-loving individual newly beginning practice, then at the very start of practice, in order to accord with realising his own true benefit, he should first abide in right mindfulness with respect to four matters, and only then go to a teacher well versed in yogic practice — whether an instructing teacher, a preceptor, or another elder or one resembling an elder worthy of respect. What are the four? First, the abode of single-mindedly seeking understanding, free of any intent to challenge or interrogate. Second, the abode of deeply arising reverence, free of arrogance. Third, the abode of seeking only what is genuinely excellent, not of displaying one's own ability. Fourth, the abode of purely establishing wholesome roots in oneself and others, not of seeking material support, honour, or renown.

items.zh: 如是正念到師處已，先求開許請問時分，然後安詳躬申請問。將請問時，偏覆左肩，右膝著地，或居下坐曲躬而坐，合掌恭敬，深生愧畏，低顏軟語請問瑜伽：我於如是瑜伽行中欲求受學，唯願慈悲，為我宣說。
items.en: Having arrived at the teacher's place with right mindfulness thus established, he should first seek permission for a time to ask his questions, and only then calmly and personally present his request. When about to ask, he covers his left shoulder, baring the right, places his right knee on the ground — or sits below the teacher with body bowed — joins his palms in reverence, gives rise to deep humility and awe, and with lowered face and gentle words requests the teaching: "In this yogic practice I wish to receive instruction; may you compassionately expound it for me."

items.zh: 如是請已；善達瑜伽諸瑜伽師，為欲安立初修業者瑜伽作意，應以慈愍柔軟言詞讚勵慶慰，又應稱揚修斷功德。歎言：善哉！善哉！
items.en: Once the request has been made in this way, the teacher well versed in yogic practice — wishing to establish the beginner's mental engagement in yoga — should praise, encourage, and console him with compassionate and gentle words, and should also extol the merit of cultivating and severing what needs to be severed. He exclaims: "Excellent! Excellent!"

items.title: Nine Praises for the Seeker, Part One: Non-Heedlessness, Seeking Liberation, Severing Bondage

items.zh: 賢首。汝今乃能於墮放逸、樂著放逸、沈沒境界、樂著境界眾生類中，獨不放逸，樂修出行。
items.en: "Excellent one! Among beings who fall into heedlessness, delight in heedlessness, are submerged in sense-objects, and delight in attachment to sense-objects, you alone are free of heedlessness and take joy in cultivating the path of release."

items.zh: 汝今乃能於久墮在種種憂苦險惡牢獄眾生類中，獨求解脫如是牢獄。
items.en: "Among beings who have long fallen into the various dangerous prisons of grief and suffering, you alone seek liberation from such a prison."

items.zh: 汝今乃能於被種種貪瞋癡等杻械枷鎖常所固縛眾生類中，獨求斷壞如是固縛。
items.en: "Among beings constantly and firmly fettered by the shackles, chains, and cangues of craving, hatred, and delusion, you alone seek to sever and break such firm bondage."

items.title: Nine Praises, Part Two: Crossing the Wilderness of Birth-and-Death, Gaining Wholesome Roots, Attaining Peace

items.zh: 汝今乃能於入生死曠野險道眾生類中，獨求超度曠野險道。
items.en: "Among beings who have entered the perilous wilderness road of birth-and-death, you alone seek to cross beyond that wilderness road."

items.zh: 汝今乃能於遭窮儉種種善根眾生類中，獨求獲得豐饒善根。
items.en: "Among beings whose various wholesome roots are impoverished and scant, you alone seek to gain abundant, flourishing wholesome roots."

items.zh: 汝今乃能於墮種種煩惱怨賊、廣大怖畏眾生類中，獨求證得究竟安隱常樂涅槃。
items.en: "Among beings who have fallen among the brigand-enemies of the various afflictions, subject to vast dread, you alone seek to attain the ultimate, peaceful, eternally blissful nirvāṇa."

items.title: Nine Praises, Part Three: Freedom from Sickness and Crossing the Floods

items.zh: 汝今乃能於為煩惱重病吞食眾生類中，獨求證得第一無病常樂涅槃。
items.en: "Among beings devoured by the grave sickness of affliction, you alone seek to attain the foremost, sickness-free, eternally blissful nirvāṇa."

items.zh: 汝今乃能於為四種瀑流漂溺眾生類中，獨求越度如是瀑流。
items.en: "Among beings swept away and drowning in the four floods, you alone seek to cross beyond such floods."

items.title: Section: The Ninth Praise — Attaining the Great Light of Wisdom

items.zh: 汝今乃能於入廣大無明黑闇眾生類中，獨求獲得大智光明。
items.en: "Among beings who have entered the vast darkness of ignorance, you alone seek to attain the great light of wisdom."

items.title: Praising the Seeker's Practice and Motivation

items.zh: 長老當知，汝若定能如是精勤修瑜伽行，乃得名為不虛受用國人信施，真實奉行如來聖教，不捨靜慮，成就勝觀，增長樂居空閑法侶，精勤修學自義瑜伽。不辱有智同梵行者。
items.en: "Elder, you should know: if you can indeed practice yogic conduct with such diligence, then you may truly be said not to squander the faithful offerings of this land's people, to genuinely carry out the Tathāgata's noble teaching, never to abandon meditative stillness, to accomplish superior insight, to help fellow companions who delight in dwelling in seclusion flourish, to diligently cultivate yogic practice for your own true benefit, and never to bring shame upon your wise fellow practitioners of the pure life."

items.zh: 汝今為欲勤修自利利他正行。汝今為欲利益安樂無量眾生，哀愍世間及諸天人阿素洛等，為令獲得義利安樂，故來問爾。
items.en: "You now, wishing to diligently cultivate the correct practice that benefits both self and others, wishing to bring benefit and happiness to countless beings, and out of compassion for this world and for gods, humans, asuras, and the rest — so that they may attain true benefit and happiness — have therefore come to ask this question."

items.zh: 以如是等柔軟言詞讚勵慶慰，稱揚修斷諸功德已，復於四種審問處法，應審問之。

items.title: Four Questions to Assess the Seeker

items.zh: 告言：長老！汝已一向歸佛法僧，非外道師及彼邪法弟子眾不？汝已最初淨修梵行、善淨尸羅、正直見不？汝已於其總摽、別辯諸聖諦法，若少、若多，聞受持不？汝於涅槃深心信解，為證寂滅而出家不？
items.en: He says: "Elder! Have you already taken refuge single-heartedly in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha, and are not a teacher of an outside path nor a disciple of its wrong teachings? Have you from the very start purely cultivated the pure conduct of celibacy, well purified your moral discipline, and formed a correct and upright view? Have you heard and upheld — whether much or little — the noble truths as both summarised and individually analysed? Do you, with deep confidence and understanding regarding nirvāṇa, go forth from home precisely to realise peaceful cessation?"

blocks.text: Fascicle 30 opens the **third yogic process** of the Śrāvaka Stage: how a beginner approaches a teacher, how the teacher examines and instructs, and the practice of calm and insight in detail, including the **nine stages of mental abiding** (九種住心), one of the most influential passages in the whole treatise.

Going, being welcomed, being questioned, being sought out; then establishing, safeguarding, seclusion, one-pointedness, and so on. Venerable Miào Jìng: "being welcomed" (慶) is the teacher's consolation and praise.

A "self-loving" beginner goes first to a teacher well versed in yoga, "whether a preceptor, a personal instructor, or another elder", with four attitudes: seeking understanding, not to challenge; reverence, not arrogance; seeking what is excellent, not to show off; and "purely establishing wholesome roots in oneself and others, not seeking material support".
"He bares his left shoulder, places his right knee on the ground", first asks permission for a time, then "with lowered face and gentle words" makes his request.

The teacher praises the seeker: among beings who are heedless, "you alone take joy in cultivating"; among those in the prison of suffering, "you alone seek release"; among those fettered by craving, hatred, and delusion; lost in the wilderness of saṃsāra; poor in wholesome roots; among the brigands of affliction; devoured by the sickness of affliction; drowning in the four floods; in the darkness of ignorance, "you alone seek the great light of wisdom". Master Cháng Bǎi: the joy of waking from the great dream of ignorance.
"If you can practise with such diligence, you will not squander the faithful offerings of this land's people." Master Cháng Bǎi: "Elder" here is a courtesy, not a matter of age.

Have you taken refuge single-heartedly in the Three Jewels? Have you kept pure conduct and discipline, with an upright view? Have you heard and upheld the noble truths, "whether much or little"? Have you gone forth "with deep confidence regarding nirvāṇa, precisely to realise peaceful cessation"? Master Cháng Bǎi: many call themselves Buddhists without having truly taken refuge.

quiz.q: "A self-loving individual newly beginning practice" — who counts as "self-loving," according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: only those who aspire to leave saṃsāra and train in the noble path
quiz.why: "If there is a self-loving individual newly beginning practice, then at the very start of practice … he should first abide in right mindfulness with respect to four matters." Venerable Miào Jìng: only those who aspire to renunciation and wish to train in the noble path are self-loving; others do not truly care for themselves.

quiz.q: "軌範師、親教師" are rendered "a preceptor, a personal instructor." How does Venerable Miào Jìng identify them?
options: 軌範師 is the ācārya, 親教師 the upādhyāya; "preceptor" usually means the latter, so the English seems swapped
quiz.why: "Only then go to a teacher well versed in yogic practice — whether a preceptor, a personal instructor, or another elder." Venerable Miào Jìng: 軌範師 is the ācārya; 親教師 is the upādhyāya, responsible for instructing you. The English gives "preceptor" for 軌範師, though "preceptor" normally renders the upādhyāya.

quiz.q: When requesting, "偏覆左肩" is rendered "bares his left shoulder." What do the masters say?
options: both: cover the left shoulder, bare the right — the English says the opposite
quiz.why: "When about to ask, he bares his left shoulder, places his right knee on the ground." Venerable Miào Jìng: the left shoulder is covered with the robe and the right shoulder bared — an Indian custom of courtesy. Master Cháng Bǎi: wear the robe covering the left shoulder, baring the right, kneel on the right knee, and first bow. The English reverses this.

quiz.q: With what words should the teacher console the beginner, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: compassionate, gentle words — not harsh ones, not three strokes of the incense board first
quiz.why: "Should praise, encourage, and console him with compassionate and gentle words, and should also extol the merit of cultivating and severing." Venerable Miào Jìng: gentle words, not harsh ones — not "let me hit you three times with the incense board first."

quiz.q: The seeker is called "賢首," rendered "Excellent one." How do the masters explain it?
options: Miào Jìng: 賢 tames body, speech, mind, 首 is wisdom leading; Cháng Bǎi: 賢 is a worthy not yet noble, 首 wisdom at the head
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: 首 is a leader — wisdom leads, guiding all actions of body, speech, and mind. Master Cháng Bǎi: 賢 is a worthy one training in the path but not yet noble; 首 means wisdom at the head. They agree on 首; on 賢, Miào Jìng says it means taming body, speech, and mind into purity.

quiz.q: How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe the joy of attaining "the great light of wisdom"?
options: like waking from the great dream of ignorance — a joy no wealth can buy
quiz.why: "You alone seek to attain the great light of wisdom." Master Cháng Bǎi: the joy of waking from the great dream of ignorance is a happiness worldly wealth cannot buy.

quiz.q: The first question: "Have you taken refuge single-heartedly?" What does Master Cháng Bǎi say about when to take refuge?
options: many wait until death, but the younger the better
quiz.why: "Have you already taken refuge single-heartedly in the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha?" Master Cháng Bǎi: many take refuge only near death, but the younger the better.
